anticolonial.works_and_arguments: The Black Jacobins now distinguishes 1938 and revised 1963; Williams’s slavery/capitalism and abolition claims remain separate and disputed. anticolonial.internal_distinctions: Six approaches separate enslaved revolution, economic slavery debates, colonial subjectivity/liberation, underdevelopment, civilizing claims and culture/class. Césaire’s polemic is not mistaken for the same kind of scholarship as Williams’s economic history; Cabral’s culture is internally differentiated rather than a timeless essence.

anticolonial.outgoing_connections: Clarified the critique of imperial narratives, James’s Marxist intervention and the different underdevelopment arguments. africanhist.people: Expanded four selections to fourteen, reusing Rodney, Ranger, Cooper and Thornton; added Johnson, Ki-Zerbo, Ogot, Hampâté Bâ, Boahen, Awe and Amadiume. africanhist.works_and_arguments: Specific works now connect regional history, oral criticism, collective synthesis, colonial perspectives, women’s research and labor. africanhist.internal_distinctions: Eleven approaches separate earlier writing, Ibadan, transmitted-source criticism, spoken knowledge, East African reconstruction, UNESCO synthesis, Dar es Salaam debates, colonized perspectives, women/gender, labor and Atlantic actors. Ranger’s retrospective rejects uniform nationalist teaching; Hampâté Bâ expressly limits his direct examples to traditions he knew.
